overclaims: The one example he gives (Fable 5, per the FT) is a report he quotes accurately.
That cuts against a literal 'dead on arrival' reading, though it predates the plateau.
checks.note: Zitron described 11% of usage; the evidence describes spending share. Calling his account accurate overlooks that difference. The evidence also does not establish that July 18 demand preceded the plateau, which began shortly after July 1.

overclaims: A September 2026 enterprise survey reported by Techstrong says cost is the main reason firms adopt open-weight models, and 60% of production users moved some workloads off proprietary models.
But proprietary use is still growing, so spending continues and there is no sign of abandonment.
checks.note: The evidence identifies cost as a key driver, without establishing it as the main reason. Growing proprietary usage does not directly establish spending. Describe the survey as consistent with part of the first stage, while distinguishing open-weight adoption from open-source spending substitution.

overclaims: OpenAI cut the Pro 200 allowance for new subscribers in late September, then doubled Pro limits on October 29.
But ChatGPT Plus usage was reported unchanged, and I found no post-publication evidence for Google or Microsoft.
ChatGPT Plus, the most common paid tier, kept its usage in the October change.
checks.note: The proposition omits the universal guarantee and changes to what a price buys. October 29 events and the October 30 report fall after the October 28 cutoff. Doubling concerned Work/Codex allowances and excluded existing Pro 200 users already on higher limits. The evidence does not establish Plus as the most common paid tier.

overclaims: OpenAI announced on September 29 that Pro 200 usage would be halved, then cancelled that cut on October 29 and doubled Pro limits.
These events fit his description for many paying users.
OpenAI's cut was reversed for existing users, which complicates the 'degradation' reading.
checks.note: The reversal occurred after the October 28 cutoff and was reported October 30. Doubling concerned specific allowances, with existing higher-limit Pro 200 users retaining theirs. The reports establish limit changes but do not establish the economic cause required by the claim and contract.
